output.brief: The drop in regular volunteers comes mainly from two changes landing together at Dock Street and Westgate. The app releases shifts to everyone on Thursdays and has no recurring bookings. Once the coordinators left on 1 May, nobody booked regulars into their usual slots. Staff bookings on behalf of volunteers fell from 74 a week to 3. Of the 213 April regulars at those two sites, 129 lost their usual slot at least twice, and 88% of them are now inactive. Millbrook has the app and a coordinator, and it is stable. Quarry Lane lost its coordinator but has no app and kept its paper roster, and it is also stable. Neither change alone explains the fall. The background-check renewal is not the cause: 21 of the 23 deactivated volunteers came back, and 121 of the 123 who lapsed held a current check. Commonplate shows only 2 of the callbacks. Low satisfaction looks like a symptom. I'm fairly confident in this. Site-level data and the booking records are consistent, though the booking records are staff-compiled. Don't cancel RotaWeave. Don't suspend the checks, which protect children. Don't purge inactive names from the roster. Instead, assign someone to book regulars into their usual slots at Dock Street and Westgate, call lapsed volunteers to offer their old slot back, and review the results after 60 days. Plan for Quarry Lane before its 6 October go-live, because it has the same gap.
